subject: Re: Reliability concerns ahead of renewal — proposed stability credit & premium onramp
messages:
From: Megan Torres <megan@fastfin.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency spikes last month — renewal conversation

Hi Logan,

Hope you're well. We ran into a few latency spikes across peak hours in April (95th/99th percentile tail events) that impacted our user-facing payment validation flows. Our SREs dug into trace IDs and we saw several transient host preemption events and a pattern of tail-latency on long context (>2k tokens) requests.

We're up for renewal in late June and this has surfaced internally as a risk. Before we talk committed spend, the execs want to understand what remediation path Redwood can offer (credits, priority routing, or a short pilot on dedicated capacity) to reduce the risk to production SLAs.

Could you share your suggested remediation and any short-term credit/error-budget offer while we evaluate expansion? CC'd procurement.

Thanks,
Megan
Megan Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, FastFin Solutions
megan@fastfin.com

--
Attachment: April-traces-summary.txt (log excerpt, referenced below)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Megan Torres <megan@fastfin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency spikes last month — renewal conversation

Megan — thanks for the level-set and the traces. I'm sorry FastFin ran into those spikes; we take tail latency seriously.

High-level proposal (short version):
- Immediate: 10% service credit applied to May invoice if error/latency thresholds you observed reoccur during the next 30 days. We can formalize as an interim addendum.
- Pilot: 6-week Dedicated Pilot (small GPU pool) focused on your payment-validation routes (pin model version + quantization profile) to show consistent p99 improvements.
- Long-term: If pilot meets targets (p99 < 350ms on typical requests), we'll provide a premium-tier onramp with a 12-month committed discount and priority capacity.

I've attached a short "Stability Credit & Pilot" proposal PDF with timelines and proposed success criteria. Ben — can you confirm the implementation work and an ops checklist we can run during the pilot? Grace, looping you for commercial/billing for the interim credit.

If that sounds reasonable, can we set a 30-minute alignment call this week? I can share an addendum draft during the call.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0199
Redwood Inference

Attachment: FF-Stability-Credit-Proposal.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Megan Torres <megan@fastfin.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency spikes last month — renewal conversation

Thanks, Logan. Quick tech notes and what we'd need for a fast pilot:

- Surface area: we should scope to the payment-validation route and any routes that share the KV-cache to avoid cache interference.
- Root cause hypothesis: the traces show periodic host preemptions + long-context attention recompute on 8k-token samples. On Dedicated we can pin instances to prevent preemption and use a slightly higher batch size with reduced tail impact.
- Data needed from FastFin: representative prompt samples (anonymized), traffic distribution across routes, and a short runway for canary traffic (5-10% traffic for 2 weeks).

Operational tasks (ops checklist):
1) Share anonymized prompt corpus (s3 link)
2) Approve model pin/version & quantization profile (we recommend q4-int8)
3) Schedule canary window and define success criteria (p50/p95/p99 targets)
4) Enable real-time tracing hooks (we'll provide the tracing integration)

We can deliver a pilot manifest and an ops-runbook within 48 hours of step 1. Happy to run the pilot tech kickoff with your SREs.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

---
On Wed, May 6, 2026 at 08:27 AM Logan wrote:
> Megan — I attached the proposal with timelines and success criteria. Ben will coordinate the ops checklist.

(Attachment: pilot-runbook-template.yml — referenced)

From: Megan Torres <megan@fastfin.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@fastfin.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 10:56:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency spikes last month — renewal conversation

Logan / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and clear plan. Procurement and I reviewed the proposal briefly. A few clarifications before we commit to the pilot:

- Can you quantify the proposed interim credit (10%) in dollar terms and the exact SLA thresholds that would trigger it? Our CFO wants a deterministic metric.
- For the Dedicated Pilot, what is the expected incremental monthly run rate (ballpark) if we choose to continue after the pilot?
- Will the pilot require us to migrate traffic (even for canary) or can you do an overlay routing approach?

We can do a 30-minute call Wednesday 5pm PT. Also, procurement wants the addendum in redline-friendly DOCX so they can start internal review.

— Megan

On a separate note: if we sign a 12-month premium onramp after proving stability, would Redwood consider a step-down credit if there's an incident above the agreed threshold in month 3? That would help our execs take the commercial step.

Megan

Attachment: procurement-request.pdf

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Megan Torres <megan@fastfin.com>, procurement@fastfin.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency spikes last month — renewal conversation

Megan — appreciate the specificity. Answering inline: 

- Interim credit: 10% of May invoice applied if a p99 latency breach (as defined in the attached proposal) recurs during the 30-day window. For determinism we'll include a metric table in the DOCX (example: p99 >= 700ms measured over 6-hour rolling windows during business hours triggers credit). We'll also include a sample dollar calculation at your request.

- Incremental run rate: For the Dedicated Pilot we estimate an incremental ~ $12k–$18k/month depending on instance size and reserved vs burst config. If you convert to a 12-month premium commitment, we'll apply a 20% committed discount (numbers in the addendum). Grace — happy to discuss exact pricing and run the model with FastFin's projected monthly tokens.

- Routing: we prefer an overlay canary (no full migration) — route 5–10% traffic to Dedicated nodes via policy rules. That avoids big traffic shifts and isolates traffic for clear signal.

- Step-down credit: yes — we can include a structured protection: if an incident above the agreed threshold occurs within the first 90 days after premium activation, Redwood will provide an additional remedial credit (pro-rated) and a one-time service health review at no charge. We'll draft the exact language in the addendum.

Next steps:
1) I'll upload a redline-ready DOCX addendum (redwood-premium-onramp-addendum.docx) to the shared link and share shortly.
2) Ben will run the tech kickoff once you share anonymized prompts.
3) Schedule Wed 5pm PT alignment call — I'll send a calendar invite.

If that aligns, we'll treat the interim credit as a short-term operational guardrail while the pilot runs.

— Logan

Attachment: redwood-premium-onramp-addendum.docx
